questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: A patient receiving chemotherapy reports a temperature of 38.1°C (100.6°F) and chills. What is the priority?
choices: Advise waiting until tomorrow's routine blood count
Prompt immediate assessment through the oncology or emergency pathway
Assume fever cannot represent infection without a cough
Recommend masking the fever before contacting the team
questions.explanation: During chemotherapy, fever at or above 38°C may be the only sign of a life-threatening infection. The patient needs immediate evaluation rather than delay for a pending blood count.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: In suspected neutropenic sepsis, which sequence best protects the patient?
choices: Wait for all cultures to become positive before treatment
Remove every central line before assessing the patient
Give only an antipyretic and reassess next shift
Assess and escalate immediately, obtain ordered specimens promptly, and administer prescribed empiric antibiotics without significant delay
questions.explanation: Neutropenic sepsis is an acute emergency. Cultures and labs support diagnosis, but collection should not meaningfully delay ordered broad-spectrum empiric antibiotics and sepsis care.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: After treatment for bulky lymphoma, potassium, phosphate, and uric acid rise while calcium and urine output fall. What syndrome should the RN suspect?
choices: Tumor lysis syndrome
Uncomplicated anemia alone
A normal expected effect with no monitoring needs
Isolated mild dehydration without renal risk
questions.explanation: Rapid tumor breakdown releases potassium and phosphate and raises uric acid, often lowering calcium and threatening renal and cardiac function. This is the classic evolving TLS pattern.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Which TLS finding requires the most urgent rhythm-focused escalation?
choices: Stable appetite after treatment
A mild change in hair texture
New ECG changes with rapidly rising potassium
A question about the next clinic appointment
questions.explanation: TLS-related hyperkalemia can cause fatal dysrhythmias. A rising potassium level with ECG changes requires immediate clinician response and prescribed cardiac and electrolyte treatment.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Which statement about urate-lowering therapy in TLS is correct?
choices: Allopurinol rapidly removes existing uric acid better than rasburicase
Allopurinol limits new uric-acid production, while rasburicase can lower existing uric acid in selected patients
Both drugs should always be given together without a risk assessment
Neither therapy requires renal or laboratory monitoring
questions.explanation: Allopurinol prevents formation of additional uric acid; rasburicase breaks down existing uric acid. The oncology team selects therapy by risk, lab trends, contraindications, and protocol.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: What is an important safety check before ordered rasburicase?
choices: Verify G6PD status or screening because deficiency increases hemolysis risk
Confirm that potassium is being added to IV fluids
Ensure the patient is taking routine urine alkalinization
Skip all uric-acid measurements after the first dose
questions.explanation: Rasburicase is contraindicated in G6PD deficiency because of hemolysis risk. Verify screening and follow pharmacy and laboratory handling instructions before administration.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Which trend best suggests that TLS treatment is effective?
choices: Rising potassium and declining urine output
Increasing creatinine with new dysrhythmia
One normal temperature despite worsening chemistry
Stabilizing electrolytes and renal function with adequate urine output and no new rhythm changes
questions.explanation: TLS improvement requires repeated assessment of potassium, phosphate, calcium, uric acid, renal function, urine output, and rhythm—not a single isolated temperature or lab value.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Why may a patient with severe neutropenia have a serious infection without obvious pus or marked local redness?
choices: Low platelets directly prevent all fevers
Antibiotics make blood cultures unnecessary
A reduced neutrophil response can blunt local inflammatory signs
Infection is impossible when the skin looks normal
questions.explanation: Neutrophils drive many typical local inflammatory findings. In profound neutropenia, fever or systemic illness may be the only early clue to infection.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: A patient at TLS risk receives ordered IV hydration and has heart failure. Which nursing monitoring is essential?
choices: Ignore intake and output until creatinine rises
Trend intake, urine output, respiratory status, edema, and chemistry for both renal protection and fluid overload
Give unlimited fluid regardless of symptoms
Add potassium to every bag unless there is an ECG change
questions.explanation: Hydration supports renal excretion in TLS, but fluid overload can harm a patient with heart failure. Closely monitor balance, urine output, breathing, and serial laboratory results.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Which patient statement shows effective febrile-neutropenia discharge teaching?
choices: I will call my cancer team right away for a temperature of 38°C or higher or if I become acutely unwell
I will wait for my next clinic visit if I develop fever
I should hide recent chemotherapy from emergency triage
A normal-looking central line proves I cannot have infection
questions.explanation: The patient should know the urgent fever or illness threshold, a 24-hour contact route, and the need to tell emergency staff about recent anticancer treatment.
